key_insight: Quantum classifiers can achieve competitive overall performance while retaining subgroup disparities, and smaller fairness gaps can mask performance losses.
clinical_relevance: Medical imaging AI should be evaluated for both subgroup disparities and preserved overall discrimination before clinical use is considered.
method: Compared SVM, MLP, QSVM and QCNN using ResNet-18 image embeddings.
Tested Equalized Odds regularisation, Gradient Reversal Learning and their combination against baseline models.
Assessed subgroup AUC gaps and a pre-specified non-inferiority margin, with PanDerm and EVA-X as external references.
evidence_signal: Audits covered DDI skin lesions by Fitzpatrick skin type and CheXpert-derived chest X-rays by age group, finding model- and dataset-dependent fairness effects.
watch_item: All quantum models ran in classical simulation; the study claims no quantum advantage.
paper_title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
